clue.text: Academic boss wanting acknowledgments of indebtedness

parts.note: a boss is a raised stud, as on a shield or a ceiling
IOUs are written notes acknowledging a debt, 'I owe you'

explanation.surface: A scholarly department head is short of thank-you notes for the people who helped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acknowledgments' suggests thanks in a book's preface, but here it means IOUs, written promises to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A studious person is bookish and given to learning, which is what an academic temperament means.

clue.text: Sidney holds set-up to be quite senseless

indicators.note: the short name wraps around the other piece, as if keeping it in its grip

parts.note: Sid is the usual short form of the name Sidney

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word for set is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to set something down is to put it

explanation.surface: Someone called Sidney is caught up in a scheme that makes no sense at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-up' reads as one noun, a scheme; split it, 'set' is the verb and 'up' turns it, the way a down answer is read upwards, and 'holds' puts that inside the short name.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupid describes something lacking sense or intelligence, entirely without reason.

clue.text: Push to produce an effect

indicators.note: to produce is to make something new, so these letters are worked into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A shove is needed to make something happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produce' makes UPSHOT from the letters of PUSH and TO.
explanation.definitionFit: The upshot of something is its final result or consequence.

clue.text: No degrees needed to be top like this!

definitions.text: No degrees needed to be top like this!

parts.words: No degrees needed to be top like this!
parts.note: the frozen covering at the top of a planet sits at zero degrees or below, and 'top' is the pole of the globe, not first place

explanation.surface: You don't need a university qualification to rise to the very top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Degrees' reads as academic qualifications; it is temperature, and 'top' is the summit of the world, its polar cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A permanent covering of ice over a polar region caps the globe where temperatures stay at or below freezing.

clue.text: Sleep on it

parts.note: the phrase normally means to delay a decision overnight; read literally it is bedding you lie on

explanation.surface: Advice to postpone a decision until morning.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'sleep on it' means think it over; taken literally it describes the bottom layer of bedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed sheet placed beneath the sleeper, over the mattress, is something one literally lies on all night.

clue.text: Very large watch made on the Continent

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
to watch over is to tend

explanation.surface: An enormous wristwatch manufactured in mainland Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like a timepiece but is the verb, to look after. 'The Continent' is the British name for mainland Europe; Ostend is a Belgian port.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostend is a ferry port in Belgium, a town on mainland Europe across the Channel from Britain.

clue.text: True art back in view

indicators.note: the turned word is placed inside the word for view

parts.note: a view is a sight

indicators.note: the word art is read backwards, going back on itself

parts.note: taken as written before being turned

explanation.surface: Genuine art returns to public display.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight and true both mean exactly in line, and also honest.

clue.text: Involves outside right-and insides

indicators.note: the word for involves sits on the outside of the single letter, enclosing it

parts.note: if one thing involves another it entails it

explanation.surface: Something that takes in the exterior, the right side, and the interior too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts ENTAILS around R.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrails are the guts or bowels, the inner organs of a body.

clue.text: Making loss, paid in settlement

indicators.note: making suggests building something new, so these letters are worked into another order

explanation.surface: A firm runs at a loss, having paid out to settle a claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making' rearranges LOSS and PAID into DISPOSAL; 'in' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A disposal is an arrangement or settling of affairs, as in property at one's disposal or the disposal of an estate.

clue.text: A French male stayed awfully insecure

parts.note: un is the masculine form of 'a' in French

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A Frenchman remained, feeling terribly uneasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A French male' points to the masculine article, and 'awfully' scrambles the word stayed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsteady is wobbly and not firmly fixed, so it is not secure.

clue.text: Talks at some length of money and taxes

parts.note: P stands for penny or pence, a unit of money
rates are local property taxes in Britain

explanation.surface: Discussions about finance and taxation drag on.
explanation.walkthrough: RATES were British local taxes on property.
explanation.definitionFit: To prate is to chatter on foolishly, going on and on.

clue.text: Adroitly affecting great love

indicators.note: affecting means altering or acting upon, so the letters of the word are changed in order

explanation.surface: A skilful performance that moves the audience deeply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affecting' rearranges ADROITLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolatry is excessive worship or devotion to someone, an extreme adoration.

clue.text: Scold when six tease duck

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
to rag someone is to tease them
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A nagging person tells off someone for teasing a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter out for no runs makes a duck, which gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: A virago is a domineering, bad-tempered woman, a shrew or nag.

clue.text: Travellers' accommodation accorded acclaim for a change

parts.note: an inn offers lodging to people on a journey
an ovation is enthusiastic applause or acclaim

explanation.surface: A hotel is applauded for doing things differently.
explanation.definitionFit: An innovation is a new method or idea, something introduced that alters the way things were done.

clue.text: Fur's needed for the cold in the Orient

indicators.note: the word for cold is placed inside the country's name

parts.note: China is a country of the Orient, the East
a chill is coldness

explanation.surface: Warm clothing is essential in the bitter Eastern winter.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinchilla is the soft grey pelt of a small South American rodent, prized for coats.

clue.text: Taking blockheads in is criminal!

parts.note: plural, so two fools, each an ass
plural, so two fools, each an ass
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fooling idiots is a crime!
explanation.walkthrough: 'blockheads' gives two ASS pieces in a row, then IN; 'Taking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a murderer, someone who kills a prominent person for political or paid reasons.

clue.text: Interfering with drainage could be a bloomer

indicators.note: interfering with something disturbs it, so the letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: Tampering with the drains might prove to be a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interfering with' rearranges DRAINAGE. A 'bloomer' looks like a blunder; it is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardenia is a fragrant white-flowered shrub, something that blooms.

clue.text: Trick the top man in similar fashion

indicators.note: the word for the top man is put inside the word for similar fashion

parts.note: done in similar fashion means done the same way
a king is the man at the top of the realm

explanation.surface: Fool the boss by copying his style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in similar fashion' looks like a link phrase; 'in' is the container signal and 'similar fashion' is the word that encloses the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin game is a swindle or confidence trick that fleeces its victims.

clue.text: Polar explorer demanding hamper to go to the North

parts.note: to shackle someone is to restrain or hamper them
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: An Antarctic adventurer insists on a picnic basket for a trip north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hamper' looks like a food basket but is the verb, to hinder. Ernest Shackleton led British expeditions to Antarctica.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Shackleton was an Anglo-Irish explorer famous for his Antarctic expeditions.

clue.text: Notes resulting from a month on the road

parts.note: Oct is the abbreviation for October
Ave, short for avenue, appears in street addresses

explanation.surface: Music written after a month of touring.
explanation.definitionFit: An octave is a series of eight musical notes spanning the interval between one note and its double.

clue.text: Go through a number with permission

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
leave is permission, as in by your leave

explanation.surface: Getting past a figure once allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave is to split or cut a way through something.

clue.text: In general the eucalyptus tree thrives in the West Country

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follow, spanning the gaps between them

explanation.surface: Gum trees generally grow well in the mild south-west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The West Country is south-west England; STREET is a village in Somerset there.
explanation.definitionFit: Street is a large village in Somerset, a county of south-west England.

clue.text: Supplying assistance is excellent-sound

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as AI
a ding is a ringing sound

explanation.surface: Providing help is a fine-sounding thing.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means first-class; its figure 1 stands in as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Aiding means helping, giving support to someone.

clue.text: The knight who's left an establishment crowd

parts.note: CE is the Church of England, the established church
a lot is a group or set of people

explanation.surface: A knight leaves the clique of the powerful.
explanation.walkthrough: The Church of England, CE, is called the Established Church. Lancelot was a knight of King Arthur's Round Table.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Lancelot was the foremost knight of Arthurian legend.

clue.text: Error committed by poor sailor

parts.note: a sin is a moral error or wrongdoing
poor quality is bad

explanation.surface: A mistake made by an unskilled seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinbad is the seafaring hero of the Arabian Nights tales, a legendary mariner.

clue.text: Address given for many years by the parson

indicators.note: by means beside, so the word for many years sits next to the clergyman

parts.note: a parson is a parish clergyman such as a vicar
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A speech delivered over many years by the local clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' looks like a speech but is where someone lives.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicarage is the house provided for a vicar, his residence.

clue.text: Possibly ten are more elegant

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Perhaps ten of them are more stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges TEN and ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Neater means tidier and more trim, smarter in appearance.

clue.text: Intrigue can bring profit

explanation.surface: Plotting can be lucrative.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrigue someone is to arouse their curiosity, and money earned on savings is a gain paid by a bank.
